column2: This tornado snapped hardwood trees while destroying one residence's shed. Metal from that shed was blown into the surrounding field. A second story of a house had much of its roof removed and had multiple interior walls collapsed. Farther east, a roof was ripped off a barn and another shed was destroyed.
column3: An EF1 tornado caused extensive damage to various buildings. A barn suffered significant damage and parts of a home were sheared away near the point of initial touchdown. Several nearby trees were snapped. As the tornado progressed, four more barns were destroyed and nearby power poles were damaged. The tornado lifted briefly for {{convert|150|yd|m|abbr=on}} before traversing ground once more, destroying an outbuilding and injuring a truck driver with the resulting debris.
column4: A tornado caused significant damage to homes south of Circleville. Multiple semi-trailers were blown over and large trees were uprooted.
column5: At least one home and a barn were damaged.
column6: One home had its second story, as well as its garage, completely destroyed. Several other homes sustained lesser structural damage. Significant and severe tree damage was observed, including some trees that were debarked. A large propane tank was thrown {{convert|20|–|30|ft|m|abbr=on}}, and a {{convert|7000|lb|kg|abbr=on}} truck was tossed into a house. A mobile home was severed in half by a fallen tree.
column7: Over 90 trees were snapped or uprooted. Several homes sustained damage due to fallen trees. A tractor trailer was overturned while a shed and other outdoor equipment was destroyed.
column8: A brief tornado caused tree damage
column9: A brief tornado snapped several trees.
column10: Upon developing, the tornado's inflow overturned a trailer and dragged it towards the twister's circulation. Several hardwood trees were snapped and several homes were damaged.
column11: The roof of a barn at a turkey farm was lofted, and 40 turkeys were killed. Outbuildings were severely damaged or destroyed, and a tractor trailer was overturned and dragged {{convert|40|ft|m|abbr=on|sortable=on}}. At least a dozen other vehicles were damaged, moved, or rolled, and many trees were snapped or uprooted with some falling on a house. Two homes sustained substantial wall damage, and others suffered roof or window damage.
column12: Dozens of trees were snapped or uprooted. A utility pole was snapped. A resident outside their home during the tornado suffered minor injuries from flying debris.
column13: A barn was unroofed and a church was damaged. Several homes and sheds were damaged.
column14: A large tornado destroyed a grain bin, outbuildings, and sheds at three farmsteads. Power poles were damaged and trees were snapped and uprooted.
column15: A tornado produced sporadic damage; two vehicles were struck by the tornado, injuring 12 before the tornado lifted.
column16: A large tornado caused major damage just south of Lawrence. News media estimated the tornado to be upwards of {{convert|1|mi|km|abbr=on}} wide before it became rain-wrapped. Vehicles were overturned on the K-10 freeway, and there was major damage to homes in the Douglas County area. A tornado emergency was issued for the town of Linwood as it made a direct hit on the town, with reports of “catastrophic” damage. A debris ball was also noted on radar. There was major damage to houses, trees, and power-lines in Douglas County and Leavenworth County. Some homes were even swept off the property. At least 18 injuries have been reported.
column17: A tornado caused significant damage to the Lenape Valley High School and injured occupants. People required rescue from the structure.
column18: Another large tornado developed from the supercell which produced the Linwood tornado. Major damage was reported to homes in Kearney
